source.document: Subaru service information (EyeSight Diagnostics General Description; Rear Bumper service info for blind spot sensor repair-prohibited area). Additional references: Subaru Pre and Post-Repair Scanning Position Statement; Opus ADAS Map inspection report (2023 Forester Wilderness).
source.note: EyeSight is camera-only — Subaru does not use a front radar. Per Subaru service info: stereo camera axis may be displaced even in a minor collision, even when the EyeSight warning light is not illuminated.

general_requirements: Per Subaru Pre/Post-Repair Scanning position: pre-repair and post-repair scanning are required. EyeSight stereo camera adjustment is required after any collision, even when no warning messages are displayed.

components.calibration_note: Use OE glass for windshield replacements. Per Subaru EyeSight service info: the stereo camera axis may be displaced even in a minor collision — calibration is required even if the EyeSight warning light is not illuminated or the Stereo Camera Temporary Stop message is not displayed. Do not apply impact or force to the stereo camera; do not disassemble, modify, or change the installation position of the camera.
triggers: Stereo camera is removed, installed, or replaced
Windshield is replaced, removed, or installed
Vehicle is in for repair after any collision, even minor (per Subaru, camera axis can be displaced without setting a warning)
Headliner or overhead console is removed, installed, or repaired in the camera mounting area

components.location: Rear Quarter Panels (behind rear bumper corners)
components.calibration_note: Subaru specifies a repair-prohibited area on the rear bumper around each blind spot sensor. If any collision trace, dent, scuff/chip, or crack is present inside that area, the rear bumper must be replaced — then check the radar installation condition and perform the radar axis adjustment. Shop practice: perform blind spot calibration when rear quarter panel is damaged in a collision, regardless of whether the sensor area itself shows visible damage.
triggers: Rear bumper has collision trace, dent, scuff/chip, or crack in the repair-prohibited area around the sensor (replace bumper, then calibrate)
Rear quarter panel is damaged in a collision
Rear quarter panel is removed, installed, replaced, or repaired in the sensor mounting area
Rear body panel is removed, installed, replaced, or repaired in the sensor mounting area
Sensor is removed, installed, or replaced
Sensor bracket is removed, installed, or replaced
Sensors are removed, installed, or replaced

components.calibration_note: Per Subaru service info: the Occupant Detection System must be calibrated and zeroed any time a seat component is removed, loosened, or replaced; the system should also be inspected after any collision.
triggers: Any seat component is removed, loosened, or replaced
Vehicle is in for repair after any accident or collision
